record.paper_title: Conferences WORDS, years 1997-2017: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: What is the minimum k such that abelian squares of period at least k can be avoided over three letters, with 2 < k < 6?

evidence.quote: What is the minimum k such that abelian squares of period at least k over three letters can be avoided (2 < k < 6)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Sigma_3 = \{a,b,c\}$ be a three-letter alphabet. A finite nonempty word $w \in \Sigma_3^+$ is called an abelian square if $w = uv$ with $|u| = |v|$ and $v$ is a permutation of $u$ (equivalently, for every letter $x \in \Sigma_3$, the number of occurrences of $x$ in $u$ equals the number in $v$). The period of such an abelian square $w = uv$ is $|u|$.

For an integer $k \ge 1$, say that an infinite word $\mathbf{w} \in \Sigma_3^{\mathbb{N}}$ avoids abelian squares of period at least $k$ if no factor of $\mathbf{w}$ is an abelian square of period $\ge k$.

It is known that no infinite word over $\Sigma_3$ avoids all abelian squares (i.e., the case $k = 1$), and it is straightforward to show that for sufficiently large $k$ such infinite words exist. Determine the minimum integer $k$ with $2 < k < 6$ such that there exists an infinite word over the three-letter alphabet $\Sigma_3$ avoiding all abelian squares of period at least $k$.
artifact.category_tag: Combinatorics on words / abelian pattern avoidance
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches surface related results on $k$-abelian square avoidance (e.g. Rao–Rosenfeld show that 2-abelian squares of period $\ge 2$ are avoidable on three letters) and on the inavoidability of all abelian squares on three letters, but no source clearly resolves the specific question of the minimum period threshold $k\in\{3,4,5\}$ for avoiding (ordinary) abelian squares of period $\ge k$ on a ternary alphabet. The question appears in a list of open problems from the WORDS conference series, and no published resolution was located.

status_evidence.title: Avoidability of long k-abelian repetitions
status_evidence.snippet: One can avoid 2-abelian-squares of period at least 2 in infinite ternary words.
status_evidence.claim: A weaker (k-abelian) version is solved on ternary, but the ordinary abelian-square period-threshold question remains unaddressed there.

status_evidence.title: Abelian Squares are Avoidable on 4 Letters
status_evidence.snippet: Infinite abelian-square-free words exist over four letters but not over three.
status_evidence.claim: Sets the context: all abelian squares cannot be avoided over three letters, motivating the period-threshold question.
